raw_response:
I'm 50 this year, and I've been farming these 20 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and add up costs myself, but most of what I know comes from doing it year after year and watching what happens on the fields around me. My household has 8 people. A couple of the younger ones work off-farm in the city and send money home, which helps, but the farm is still what feeds us. I have a well, so I can pump water when the rain doesn't come.

For winter wheat, I plant the full 20 mu. Last year I used an improved variety from the seed dealer in town—not some fancy new name, but a reliable one that gave me about 550 kg per mu. I will rotary till the land after the maize harvest, then sow in October. For fertilizer, I put down 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, the kind with 16-16-16 printed on the bag, as base fertilizer at sowing time. Then at jointing in spring, I spread another 20 kg per mu of urea. That works out to about 17 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphate, and 8 kg of potash per mu. I know that is a bit heavy, but last year when my neighbor cut back his wheat turned yellow and thin. I'd rather spend the extra few hundred yuan than risk that. I irrigate three times: the overwintering water before freeze-up, the jointing water in March or April, and one more at grain filling. I spray three times—herbicide once in early spring, then fungicide and insecticide around heading time because the weather gets humid and diseases come fast. I hire the machinery team for rotary tilling and seeding. Twenty mu is too much to do by hand, and their prices are fair.

For summer maize, I also plant 20 mu right after wheat harvest in early June. I use hybrid seed—usually Zhengdan 958 or whatever the dealer says is moving well that year. I don't plow for maize; I use the no-tillage planter that drills right into the wheat stubble. That saves diesel and two days of work, and the sowing window is short so you can't waste time. I apply 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting—I get the 20-10-10 formula from the dealer—and then side-dress 15 kg per mu of urea when the plants hit the big trumpet stage. That gives me about 16 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphate, and 5 kg of potash per mu. I irrigate twice: once when the plants are knee-high if June is dry, and again at tasseling in July. The summer rains usually help, but you can't count on them. I spray twice: herbicide right after sowing, and then insecticide for corn borer in mid-July. If the weather holds I expect 650 kg per mu.

I think about the whole budget. The fertilizer bill is big for 20 mu, but it is my main investment. Last year I tried to save money by skipping one pesticide spray, and I ended up paying more for hired labor to deal with the weed problem. Never again. I watch what the other farmers with 15 to 20 mu do, and we mostly copy each other. If everyone is putting on one bag per mu, I do too. A bad harvest means losing tens of thousands of yuan; wasting a little fertilizer is just a few hundred yuan. The choice is easy.
